_meta.status: adopted 2026-10-29 under di Mino's delegation ("use your judgement here"), with the three rules added after the Luwian pilot; binds from C1
_meta.rule: One articulatory table for every arm, the controls and the nulls. A phoneme maps by place and manner, never by fit to any Linear A form. ZERO = written with the bare vowel sign (no consonant series).
decided_here_where_the_protocol_is_silen: Labial fricative f (Egyptian, Hurrian) → P: the nearest series by place; Linear B writes Greek ph with P.
Aspirates ph, th, kh, kʷh → the series of their plain stop (P, T, K, Q), as Linear B writes them.
Voiced interdental ḏ (Semitic) → T: the protocol names plain d alone for D, and interdentals for T.
Egyptological ṯ and ḏ (palatal affricates) → T: nearest stop series by place; no palatal series exists.
Velar and uvular fricatives ḫ, ġ, Egyptian ẖ → K: same place as the velar and uvular stops; they are neither laryngeal nor pharyngeal.
Luwian and Hittite cuneiform ḫ / h, ḫḫ (laryngeals) → ZERO.
Luwian and Hurrian z (affricate /ts/) and Greek z → Z, by the protocol's own z → Z.
Egyptian ꜣ (aleph) → ZERO; Egyptian j → J everywhere (one mechanical rule, though j is sometimes an aleph).
Semitic and Egyptian w, y/j → W, J; Greek digamma w → W.

A doubled consonant (tt, ss, mm, hh, Luwian fortis), whether a builder wrote it as one segment or two, renders as one consonant of its series: Linear B writes no gemination (added after the 2026-10-29 Luwian pilot).

Yakubovich's capital T, a cover symbol for fortis t(t) or lenis d where the grammar cannot tell them apart (p. 16), → T: the grammar names it by t, and the series must not depend on the renderer's guess (added after the pilot).

Before mapping, adjacent segments that together spell a multi-letter key of this map (g+w, k+w, t+s, p+h, t+h, k+h) are joined, so the series never depends on whether a builder split a digraph (the Codex and Claude Luwian builds differ only in g-w-a vs gw-a).
_meta.vowels: a e i o u map to themselves; long vowels map to their short vowel; ə → e; Egyptian filler vowel per §13 item 7; diphthongs written as two signs (V + J/W) except where the arm's edition writes them as one vowel.
